title: Cartan decomposition for a split reductive model over a DVR
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $L$. Let $\mathcal D$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine finite-type $R$-group scheme, with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Suppose its geometric fibres are reductive: over an algebraically closed field this means smooth, connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], affine of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup; unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Let $\mathcal T\subseteq\mathcal D$ be a closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion] isomorphic to $\mathbf G_{m,R}^{r}$, for an integer $r\geq0$, whose geometric fibres are maximal tori. Here $\mathbf G_{m,R}=\operatorname{Spec}R[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units, and a torus over an algebraically closed field is a finite product of $\mathbf G_m$. Put $G=\mathcal D\times_R\operatorname{Spec}L$ and $T=\mathcal T\times_R\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For an $R$-algebra $S$, points mean $R$-scheme morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\mathcal D$, with group law induced by multiplication. Identify $\mathcal D(R)$ and $T(L)$ with their images in $G(L)$. Then for every $g\in G(L)$ there exist $k_1,k_2\in\mathcal D(R)$ and $t\in T(L)$ such that $g=k_1tk_2$. No completeness or local compactness assumption on $L$ is required.

source.place: WANTED locally; author-hosted PDF https://sites.math.washington.edu/~jarod/papers/iwahori.pdf, Theorem 4.1 and Remark 4.2, printed p.7, together with the fixed-torus formulation in Remark 3.5, printed p.5.

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ and put $\widehat R=\varprojlim R/(\pi^n)$. The completion-DVR node makes $\widehat R$ a DVR, the local-completion node identifies its maximal ideal as $\pi\widehat R$ and its residue field as $R/(\pi)$, and module-completion completeness gives $\widehat R/(\pi^n)\simeq R/(\pi^n)$ and completeness. The map $R\to\widehat R$ is injective: a nonzero $a=u\pi^m$ has nonzero image modulo $\pi^{m+1}$. Thus $L\hookrightarrow\widehat L=\operatorname{Frac}(\widehat R)$. Moreover $L\cap\widehat R=R$: write $x\in L^\times$ as $u\pi^j$ with $u\in R^\times$, $j\in\mathbf Z$; a negative $j$ cannot be integral in the DVR $\widehat R$, because $\pi$ is not a unit there. This also covers $x=0$.

Base change $\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal T$ to $\widehat R$. Smoothness and finite type persist by the two cited base-change statements. Affineness follows from the affine fibre-product formula; the closed torus remains closed because its coordinate-ring surjection remains surjective on tensoring (each tensor is a sum of lifted pure tensors). The group diagrams and the chosen torus splitting base change. A geometric fibre of the new model is a geometric fibre after scalar extension of the original one, so the assumed reductivity and maximality still hold. Apply the complete-DVR cocharacter factorization to $g$, and then integral conjugacy into $\mathcal T_{\widehat R}$: absorbing the conjugating element and its inverse into the two integral factors gives $g=a\nu(\pi)b$, where $a,b\in\mathcal D(\widehat R)$ and $\nu:\mathbf G_{m,\widehat R}\to\mathcal T_{\widehat R}$.

source.place: Theorem 1.3 (1) to (3), Remark 3.5, and start of Theorem 4.1 proof, printed pp.5-7.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal D=\operatorname{Spec}A$, with $A$ generated over $R$ by $x_1,\ldots,x_s$. The affine fibre-product formula identifies its generic coordinate ring with $A\otimes_R L=A[1/\pi]$. Conjugation $c_t:h\mapsto tht^{-1}$ is an $L$-group automorphism. For each $j$ choose $m_j\geq0$ and $y_j\in A$ with $c_t^*x_j=y_j/\pi^{m_j}$ in $A[1/\pi]$, and put $N=1+\max(0,m_1,\ldots,m_s)$. If $e\in\mathcal D(\widehat R)$ reduces to $1$ modulo $\pi^N$, then $y_j(e)-y_j(1)\in\pi^N\widehat R$. Since $c_t(1)=1$, the equality in $\widehat L$ is $x_j(c_t(e))=x_j(1)+(y_j(e)-y_j(1))/\pi^{m_j}\in\widehat R$. The generators therefore show that the coordinate map of $c_t(e)$ has image in $\widehat R$, so $c_t(e)\in\mathcal D(\widehat R)$. This gives the precise bound needed below, with no matrix embedding or topology theorem.

source.place: Theorem 4.1 proof, approximation error and conjugation, printed p.7; agent affine-coordinate denominator calculation.

proof.text: The quotient comparison of step 1 identifies the reduction of $b$ modulo $\pi^N$ with a point of $\mathcal D(R/(\pi^N))$. Apply reduction-surjectivity to $R$, $J=(\pi^N)$ and the given split reductive model: $R$ is a Noetherian local ring and $J$ is contained in its maximal ideal. Obtain $k\in\mathcal D(R)$ with the same reduction as $b$. Set $e=bk^{-1}$; the group law commutes with reduction, so $e\equiv1\pmod{\pi^N}$. Step 4 yields $c_t(e)\in\mathcal D(\widehat R)$, and hence $g=at e k=a c_t(e)t k$. Put $h=a c_t(e)=gk^{-1}t^{-1}$, which lies both in $\mathcal D(\widehat R)$ and in $G(L)$.

source.place: Theorem 4.1 proof, approximation of the right factor and absorption of the conjugated error, printed pp.7-8; agent uses full split-group quotient lifting instead of only opposite-root coordinates.

proof.text: The affine coordinate map of $h\in G(L)$ sends $A$ into $L$, and, since the same point is in $\mathcal D(\widehat R)$, sends $A$ into $\widehat R$ inside $\widehat L$. Step 1 gives $L\cap\widehat R=R$, so this map has image in $R$ and defines $h\in\mathcal D(R)$. Equality of the two generic points implies equality of their coordinate maps because $L\hookrightarrow\widehat L$ is injective. Thus $g=htk$ with $h,k\in\mathcal D(R)$ and $t\in T(L)$, as required. The argument uses completion as an auxiliary ring, so imposes no completeness or local compactness on the original field.

source.place: Last paragraph of Theorem 4.1 proof, printed p.8: intersection of rational and completed integral points.
